acceptance: The writer is identified or the edits are recorded as unattributed with evidence checked
The edits live in a worktree or were deliberately dropped by their owner
git status in the primary clone is empty
context:
Found 2026-10-20 during the follow-up batch. Evidence is from that session; re-verify before editing. Unclaimed.

2026-10-27 21:19Z: another occurrence. Uncommitted edits to tests/unit/scripts/oracle_reviewers/conftest.py and test_attempt_loop.py in the primary clone made the pr-preflight pre-push hook refuse every worktree push until they were cleared about 13 minutes later. Not written by the docs migration session. Earlier in the docs migration, delegated agents also leaked edits into the primary clone through relative paths several times; each was reverted.

2026-10-30 data point: a delegated subagent told to work in its own worktree made its first edit (one line in docs/internal/adr/adr-site-repo-split.md) at the primary clone's absolute path. It noticed, restored the line by hand, reapplied the change in the worktree, and the primary was clean afterwards. So in-session subagents using absolute primary-clone paths are one source of primary-clone writes, not only concurrent sessions; the edit tool does not refuse such paths.

2026-10-31 data point: at 11:19:22 local, benchbox/core/benchmark_loader.py in the primary clone gained a broken partial of a change that landed 10 s later in the worktree BenchBox.wt-dep-errors (branch fix/benchmark-dependency-errors), another session. The dirty-primary guard then refused commits in every worktree until that session restored the file at 11:22:03. Same pattern as 2026-10-30: an agent edit addressed to the primary clone's absolute path just before the intended worktree edit.

2026-10-31/11-01, two more incidents: (1) a delegated worker on BenchBox PR #3886 ran its first edit command with a relative path from the primary clone's directory, so the edit landed in the primary clone; it reverted that one file with git checkout and git status was clean afterwards. (2) While another worker ran make pr-open, the primary clone held another session's uncommitted edits to benchbox/cli/commands/*.py (about host_guarded); pr-open refused until they disappeared about two minutes later.

2026-11-01: still recurring. During the oracle batch the primary clone gained stray uncommitted edits at least four times (including query_normalizer.py and write_primitives/benchmark.py), blocking agent preflight; each time the diff was saved to /Users/joe/Developer/benchbox-main-clone-<UTC>.patch and the files restored.

2026-11-04 and 2026-11-05 evidence: in feature-delivery batches, member sessions wrote to the primary clone because the file tools resolve relative paths against the session cwd, which is the primary clone, rather than against the member worktree. On 2026-11-04, Doris and Databend members left uncommitted edits in benchbox/platforms/databend/adapter.py, doris.py and tests/unit/platforms/test_doris_*.py; on 2026-11-05, a reference-doc member edited docs/internal/throughput-result-alignment.md. Both were moved into the worktrees and reverted. An explicit broadcast instruction to use absolute paths did not prevent the second case. Possible guard: make batch-member-check (and member-create) refuse while the primary clone is dirty, or the harness starts member sessions with cwd set to their worktree.

2026-11-07: guard shipped in PR #4027 (merge b097f00fdd): make batch-member-create and make batch-member-check refuse while the primary clone has uncommitted tracked changes, naming the files and the likely cause (an edit through a path that resolves to the primary clone) with the move-and-restore recipe; the existing in-scope check, including untracked files, still runs first. Tests in test_batch_integration.py. This item stays open: its acceptance (writer identified or edits recorded as unattributed, edits in a worktree or dropped by their owner, primary status empty) concerns the original 2026-10-20 incident and later recurrences, which this change does not resolve.
description: The dirty-primary guard (merged 2026-10-20) now fails commits in every worktree while the primary has uncommitted changes. At 19:20 EDT on 2026-10-20 three tracked files appeared modified (written 2 s apart, after all batch workers had reported idle): _project/decisions/sqlglot-soft-fork-plan.md, docs/development/adr/adr-sql-compat-phase-aware-pipeline.md, docs/development/adr/adr-sqlglot-use-and-non-use.md (16 lines added). Related worktrees exist: BenchBox.wt-adr-ownership, wt-checker-wrapper, wt-sqlglot-floor-residual. Work: identify the writer (session history, the worktree for branch docs/adr-sqlglot-fork-ownership), move the edits into that worktree, and confirm the primary is clean. Never discard another session's edits. Also decide whether the guard needs a clearer message pointing at the likely cause.
